chapter: Early bands, Calloway to Basie and Kansas City (third typescript)
title: Written arrangements, heads and copying solos in the early bands
summary: Early bands used written parts and heads; improvised solos were often copied from others, and Louis Armstrong's phrases turn up in everyone's solos.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Yeah -- well the level -- on some of them the level is self adjusting and (inaudible). These bands that we've been talking about -- the early bands that you played in -- did they have mostly -- if they had arrangements were they heads or did they play from written --
Some of them had written things -- some had (inaudible). (Inaudible).
And mostly each bandhad its own -- at least tried to have its own style (inaudible).
Everybody had their own (inaudible) -- thought they were hot stuff -- everybody (inaudible).
Would there be much of what you might call improvised solo playing in those days -- I imagine it would be mostly a matter of taking a break or a few bars or something.

Yes. There was much improvising. And a lot of times -- you know -- guys would take something somebody else had played they'd heard played -- you know -- put it in there. It's like they used to play a regular trombone solo on -- they thought it was a really great thing to do you know. Play it -- sing on the road.

And if it was a masterpiece thing -- everyone wants to play it today -- they try to play (singing) -- but you know invariably they'd want to play his solo. Everybody -- you know -- but it's (inaudible) they're playing really. It's a nostalgic theme and it's -- and it's like Tommy Dorsey playing -- everyone wants to play it exactly like they play it.
That's the way it was in those days, too. You hear somebody playing something and you know -- copy it. They'd help them around like that a good deal.
And then the guy who copied it would be the one who became famous for it --
